pick.title: Semester-Long Memory for Course Assistants
pick.abstract: Course assistants built on LLMs forget each student between sessions. We give an assistant a per-student memory that it summarises after every session and retrieves at the start of the next, and deploy it in two introductory programming courses (n = 412) for a full semester. Compared with a stateless assistant, the memory assistant resolved 18% more follow-up questions without a TA, and students rated its answers as more relevant to their own code. Students also reported discomfort when the assistant recalled past mistakes unprompted.
pick.why: Per-student memory deployed in university courses for a full semester, where both Interests meet.
pick.summary: After each session the assistant wrote a 200-word summary of the student's goals, misconceptions and code and retrieved the last three next time; over 9,870 sessions follow-ups resolved without a TA rose from 61% to 79%, while 23% of interviewed students said recalled mistakes felt like surveillance.
